```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(epidemiologysuite)
```

Epidemiological suite has two faces: an interactive app and a set of R functions. They share the same formulas, so a number
you read in the app is the number the function returns.

## The app

```{r app, eval = FALSE}
library(epidemiologysuite)
run_app()                                  # opens the app in your browser
run_app(calculator = "eyes per patient")   # opens it on one calculator
```

The Home page has a search box, quick links and a guided wizard ("Not sure which calculator?"). Every calculator has a *Calculate*
tab, a *Formula / Help* tab with a worked example, and a *Reference* tab naming the source of the formula.

## Finding a calculator from R

`ss_find()` searches the same list as the app's search box. Every word you give must match somewhere in the design's name, the
question it answers or the calculator that holds it; results are ranked by how well they match.

```{r find}
ss_find("eyes per patient")[, c("key", "calculator")]
ss_find("kappa", n = 3)[, c("key", "design")]
```

The `key` can be given to `run_app(calculator = )`. In RStudio or Positron the addin *Find a sample size calculator* does the same
from a small window.

## Every calculation is a function

All 195 `calc_*()` functions are exported, each with a help page (`?calc_means_paired`) that describes every argument and the value, and
ends with a worked example that is also a test.

```{r calc}
res <- calc_proportion_precision(p = 0.5, d = 0.05)
res
```

A result is a list of class `ss_result`: the headline number first, then the other components, then `inputs`, the arguments the result
was calculated from.

```{r result}
names(res)
res$inputs
```

Results are reproducible: designs that simulate take a `seed`, and the same seed gives the same answer.

## Citing

```{r cite}
citation("epidemiologysuite")
```

The app's *Cite* tab gives the same citation in APA, Vancouver, Harvard, IEEE, MLA, Chicago, BibTeX and RIS. Each calculator's
*Reference* tab also names the original source of its formula; please cite those where you report a calculation.
